result.summary: Manual review of the two supplied files, `vscode-plugin/src/connections/__tests__/feedback.test.ts` and `vscode-plugin/src/connections/messages.ts`. I found no concrete, reachable defect in either. The test asserts the right behaviors: product icons for every driver, an icon picker with keyboard navigation, safe message history capped at 200, and per-row removal. For per-row removal it covers dirty-draft cancel making zero requests, a stale-row refusal, and a rejected `method` field. `messages.ts` is a frozen table of fixed safe strings with no interpolation of private data. The code under test was not supplied: host, renderer, gateway, datasource-icons, types, fixtures, the Kotlin side, `plugin.xml` and `extension.ts`. So every assigned obligation is could-not-verify, and none is marked holds. The tests give indirect evidence for a few of them, but the implementation was not inspected. This is not a canonical CR and does not approve BUILD.

obligations.evidence: The shared model, controller, wire and Kotlin counterpart were not supplied. The test (feedback.test.ts:50-52, 82) only indirectly shows that messages are host-authoritative, that the renderer makes no sink calls (`dom.sinkCalls.length===0`), and that the synthetic renderer message projection is not accepted. Memory-only and no-persistence properties are not demonstrated beyond that.

The test (feedback.test.ts:58-76) shows these removal behaviors. Dirty cancel and confirm-cancel send zero requests. The confirmation names the target row. A stale remove-row intent is refused with the confirmation staying null. A `method` field is rejected by `parseConnectionIntent`. The removal module (`ConnectionRemovals`) was not supplied. The cleanup-phase status card, ticket-only retry and conflict reconfirmation were not evidenced.
No Kotlin or JetBrains files were supplied. VS Code only.

The test covers one case: a per-row Delete on a dirty draft prompts, and Cancel keeps the draft and the focused row with zero requests (feedback.test.ts:67-68). Root, filter and scope change, panel close and unknown-operation retention were not evidenced.
The pure model and reducer were not supplied. The tests only touch host and renderer behavior such as list state 'empty-registry', row selection and the confirmation state.
No unsupported-file or resource-limit handling was in the supplied files.
No test run results, sweep records or manual evidence were supplied. The focused test file exists. User-reported VS Code manual testing is not independently documented here.

The tests exercise a fake-panel injected host, a masked and disabled kind field, escaped message text (the `` payload yields zero img elements), the dialog focus return, and the picker's ARIA roles. The renderer, CSP and host source were not supplied. Strict-message and CSP acceptance cannot be confirmed.
No `extension.ts`, manifest or command wiring was supplied.
The tests show that message history survives a manager reopen (feedback.test.ts:50-52). No live lifecycle, lease, disposal or drain evidence was supplied.
No artifacts, gate or inventory files were supplied.

limitations: Only a new test file and a constants file were supplied. The host, renderer, gateway, datasource-icons, types, fixtures, shared removal and controller modules were not visible.
The hard-coded picker option count of 29 and the icon manifest checks depend on assets and a corpus that were not supplied. I could not confirm they agree.
No Kotlin, plugin.xml, extension.ts or manifest files were supplied. JetBrains and entry-point obligations are unassessed.
No test run output was supplied. I did not judge whether the tests pass.
All changed files in the batch were read. Their depth of assessment is limited to their own content.
